name: The Germs That Changed History
description: Plague, smallpox, cholera and flu: how microbes toppled empires, how scientists learned to fight them, and the diseases that still threaten us.

checkpoints.name: The old scourges
checkpoints.note: Smallpox, measles and other ancient diseases shape life long before anyone knows what causes them.

checkpoints.name: Plague and pox
checkpoints.note: The Black Death kills millions, syphilis spreads through Europe and Edward Jenner tries the first vaccine.

checkpoints.name: The germ theory
checkpoints.note: Cholera and the potato blight devastate whole countries, and Pasteur and Koch prove that germs cause disease.

checkpoints.name: Vaccines and pandemics
checkpoints.note: Flu in 1918 and HIV in the 1980s show new threats, while vaccines and antibiotics bring polio and others under control, and smallpox is wiped out.

checkpoints.name: New outbreaks
checkpoints.note: SARS, Ebola and COVID-19 show how fast a virus can travel in a connected world, and how quickly a vaccine can now be made.
